note: Svalbard Energi AS (Longyearbyen's municipal utility), notice updated 2025-09-25: from 1 Oct 2025 households pay 1.20 kr/kWh flat, any consumption, fixed charge included; before: 3.20 kr/kWh + about 10.50 kr/day (at 300 kWh/month: 3.20 + 10.50 x 30.4 / 300 = 4.26). Revised national budget May 2026 keeps a Svalbardpris for 2026 (NOK 9.3m) so households pay what a mainland Norgespris household pays. Covers Longyearbyen (about 2,500 of Svalbard's residents); Barentsburg (Russian mining settlement) and Jan Mayen (station staff) not priced

licence: press report of an official tariff decision
note: 200 x 300 = 60,000 old YER (about US$112 at ~535 old YER/USD), so 300 YER/kWh. Raised from 250 to 300 per kWh (reported 2026-10-01, Khabar, an outlet hostile to the Sana'a authorities; decision text not seen). Earlier steps: 257 commercial-generator cap (Nov 2023), tiered public tariff 230 for 1-2,999 kWh per half-month (Sep 2024, https://yemeneco.org/archives/81651). Chosen because most Yemenis live in Sana'a-controlled areas and grid power there is sold at this level; the Aden-side grid tariff is 19 new YER/kWh (Ministry memo Jul 2026, https://south24.net/news/newse.php?nid=5623) but supplies a few hours a day and much of the south also buys from private generators. The two rials share the code YER but trade at ~535 vs ~1,600 per USD: the pipeline's YER rate (Frankfurter, 266 per EUR) matches neither, see averages.md
